newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil supreme court again delays telecom ruling.
newsitem.headline: Brazil supreme court again delays telecom ruling.

text.p: Brazil's supreme court has again delayed ruling on the constitutionality of the government's telecommunications privatization program after a judge requested more time to study the case, an official said.
The official said no new date had been set for resumption of the case, which began in February and has been delayed on several occasions.
The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) only meets for full sessions on Wednesdays and Thursdays and is unlikely to rule next week because of the Easter holiday.

The STF is mulling the constitutionality of a so-called Minimum Telecommunications Law which the government introduced in 1996 as a legal framework for its plan to tender out concessions to run B Band cellular services.
A ruling against the law could put on hold the government's plan to begin the B Band concession program April 7, when bids from would-be operators are due in.
